review_notes: I read the whole target theorem and the definitions it depends on: explicitMap2_mk, explicitMap2Equiv_apply and cocyclesMap2_apply in ExplicitFunctoriality.lean, explicitInfl2_mk in Inflation/Basic.lean, and cohomFpAddEquivH2_cohomFpMap in TrivialFp/Explicit.lean. I also grepped uses across the repository. The file adds no simp lemmas of its own. The one issue I found is in the simp interface of an imported lemma. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether making the lemma simp would cause problems. The proof's own comments suggest the rewrites are fragile when the continuity or equivariance proof arguments differ.

findings.problem: The pointwise evaluation lemma `cocyclesMap2_apply` has no `@[simp]` attribute. Its sibling lemmas `explicitMap2_mk`, `explicitMap2Equiv_apply` and `explicitInfl2_mk` are all `@[simp]` and produce `cocyclesMap2 ... c` terms. A simp set therefore stops at a coerced `cocyclesMap2` that it cannot evaluate. Callers must name the lemma by hand, as here with `rw`, in `simp only [..., cocyclesMap2_apply, ...]` in RelabelQuotient.lean, and in `rw [finiteLevelZ2, cocyclesMap2_apply, ...]` in CrossedProduct/Inflation.lean. Its statement is a standard normal form: a coerced cocycle pullback applied to `(h, k)` rewrites to `f (c (φ h, φ k))`. It is proved by `rfl`, and the right side is strictly simpler, with no loop.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `cocyclesMap2_apply` in ExplicitFunctoriality.lean with `@[simp]`. It has the same shape as the existing simp lemmas `explicitMap2_mk` and `explicitInfl2_mk`. The `rw [cocyclesMap2_apply, cocyclesMap2_apply]` step at line 70 could then become `simp only [cocyclesMap2_apply]`, or a plain `simp`. Check that the simp-normal form still matches the `exact` step on lines 71–73. If the explicit-argument unification problems noted in CupProduct.lean and GroupExtension/Cohomology.lean still arise, keep the manual terms there.
findings.benefit: The chain `explicitMap2_mk` → `cocyclesMap2_apply` would then be a complete simp rewrite from explicit maps on classes to pointwise cocycle values. Proofs like this one would not need to name the evaluation lemma, and repeated `rw [cocyclesMap2_apply, cocyclesMap2_apply]` calls would collapse. The several downstream proofs that already import it could use `simp` directly.
